{{Quote|Subspace is clear. If we wanted, we could send a signal all the way to the Trigaskian Blur.|Tripp|<ref name="Mindor">''[[Luke Skywalker and the Shadows of Mindor]]''</ref>}}
The '''Trigaskian Blur''' was a location in [[Realspace/Legends|space]]<ref name="Mindor" /> that was situated within [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]],<ref name="EAOC" /> relatively far from the<ref name="Mindor" /> [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]]<ref name="EAOC Mindor">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}} &mdash; Based on corresponding data for [[Taspan system]]</ref> [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Mindor/Legends|Mindor]]. When the [[Mindor resistance]] leader [[Aeona Cantor]] asked her fellow insurgent [[Tripp (Mindor)|Tripp]] about the status of [[Subspace/Legends|subspace]] [[Jammer/Legends|jammers]] that the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] [[Cronal|Shadowspawn]] had installed on Mindor<ref name="Mindor" /> in the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[5 ABY/Legends|5 ABY]],<ref name="TERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref> Tripp replied that the jammers were inoperative, adding that the resistance could send a subspace signal across the considerable distance between the planet and the Trigaskian Blur if they wanted to.<ref name="Mindor" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Trigaskian Blur was first mentioned in the [[2008]] novel ''[[Luke Skywalker and the Shadows of Mindor]]'', written by [[Matthew Stover]],<ref name="Mindor" /> and was placed in grid square W-10 by the [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]''.<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>
